title: PruneGNN: Algorithm-Architecture Pruning Framework for Graph Neural Network Acceleration
problem: GNNs face tight latency constraints with massive, unstructured, sparse graphs. Irregular pruning techniques fail to exploit parallelism on vectorized hardware due to diminished sparse matrix multiplication performance, while existing structured pruning introduces scalability challenges that prevent exploiting full GPU parallelism potential.
motivation: Real-world GNN applications require acceleration under tight latency constraints, but existing pruning approaches either sacrifice exploitable parallelism or introduce architectural inefficiencies.
method: PruneGNN combines dimension-pruning-aware sparse training at the algorithm level with SIMD-aware custom kernels at the architecture level. The algorithm achieves high sparsity while maintaining accuracy through dimension-aware training. Custom kernels exploit matrix-operator-level parallelism to unlock performance gains from reduced-dimension GNN models on GPU vectorized hardware.
key_novelty: SIMD-aware kernels that exploit matrix-operator-level parallelism to overcome the diminished parallelism of both irregular and prior structured pruning approaches on vectorized GPUs.
contributions: Quantitative analysis showing irregular sparsity cannot be exploited on vectorized parallel architectures
Dimension-pruning-aware sparse training method achieving high sparsity with maintained accuracy
Novel SIMD-aware kernels exploiting matrix-operator-level parallelism for reduced-dimension models
2x average speedup over prior structured pruning methods on NVIDIA A100
baselines: prior structured pruning work for GNNs
limitations: Evaluation limited to NVIDIA A100 GPU; generalization to other hardware platforms and scalability to larger graphs not discussed.
primary_theme: structured pruning and SIMD-aware kernel optimization for GNN acceleration
